subtitle: Red chile pork tamales
verso: Whoever's born to be a tamal, the husks fall to him from heaven.
story: Tamales are a group effort. The tamalada, usually before Christmas, puts the whole family at the table spreading masa. Red pork tamales are the classic.

ingredients.title: The filling
items: 2½ lb pork shoulder, in large chunks
½ onion, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp salt
8 chiles guajillo
3 chiles ancho
2 garlic cloves, ½ tsp cumin and ½ tsp Mexican oregano
2 tbsp lard

ingredients.title: The masa
items: 4 lb fresh unprepared masa for tamales (from a tortilla shop), or 6 cups masa harina for tamales mixed with about 5 cups warm broth
2 cups (450 g) fresh pork lard, not hydrogenated
2 tsp baking powder
1 tbsp salt
1–2 cups warm pork broth
½ cup of the red chile sauce, for color

ingredients.title: The husks
items: 60 dried corn husks, soaked in hot water 1 hour

steps: Cover the pork with water, add the onion, garlic and salt, and simmer 2 hours until tender. Shred and keep the broth.
Toast, soak and blend the chiles with the garlic, cumin, oregano and [[1½ cups]] broth. Strain.
Fry the sauce in the lard 5 minutes. Set aside [[½ cup]] for the masa. Add the pork to the rest and simmer 15 minutes until thick, not soupy. Let cool.
Beat the lard with a mixer 3–5 minutes until white and fluffy.
Add the masa a handful at a time, alternating with the broth, baking powder, salt and reserved chile. Beat 10 minutes. It should feel like soft peanut butter.
Do the float test: drop ½ tsp of masa into a glass of cold water. If it floats, it's ready. If it sinks, beat longer or add a little more lard.
Take a husk, smooth side up, wide end toward you. Spread 2–3 tbsp masa thinly over the top two-thirds, leaving a border at the sides. Add a spoonful of filling.
Fold the sides over each other, then fold the narrow tail up.
Fill the bottom of a tamalera with water below the rack. Stand the tamales upright, open end up. Cover with extra husks and a damp towel, then the lid.
Steam over medium 1¼–1½ hours. They're done when the husk peels away cleanly from the masa. Let rest 15 minutes before serving.

pressureCooker.time: 25 min high pressure + 15 min natural release
steps: Make the filling and masa and assemble the tamales as above. The pork can also go under pressure: 35 minutes high, natural release 10.
Put the trivet in the pot with 1½ cups water. Stand the tamales upright, open end up, snug but not tight. A 6-qt pot holds 12–15.
High pressure 25 minutes, natural release 15.
Let rest 10 minutes. They firm up as they cool.
pressureCooker.note: Reheat frozen tamales at high pressure 15 minutes with 1 cup water.

tips: Drop a coin in the water under the rack. While it rattles there's water; when it goes quiet, add more hot water.

Grandmas say tamales have feelings: make them while angry and they won't cook through, and lift the lid too often and they come out pintos (half raw). A pregnant helper ties a red ribbon around her belly, and some cooks sing to the pot.
The old way to leaven: instead of baking powder, boil tomatillo husks with a pinch of tequesquite, strain, and beat that water into the masa.
Fresh lard from the butcher makes the masa taste right. The white blocks from the supermarket shelf don't.

variations.name: Tamales de Rajas con Queso
variations.subtitle: Poblano strip and cheese tamales
variations.note: The meatless favorite, for Lent or for anyone.

items: Masa from the base, made without the chile and with chicken or vegetable broth
4 poblanos, roasted, peeled and cut in strips
12 oz queso Oaxaca or panela, in sticks
1 cup salsa verde

steps: Spread masa on each husk.
Add a few poblano strips, a stick of cheese and a spoonful of salsa verde.
Fold and steam as in the base.
variations.pressureNote: Same as the base: high pressure 25 minutes, natural release 15.

variations.name: Tamales de Dulce
variations.subtitle: Sweet pink tamales
variations.note: Sweet tamales for Christmas and Día de la Candelaria, served with champurrado. On February 2, whoever found the baby figurine in the Rosca de Reyes on January 6 pays for the tamales.

items: 2 lb fresh masa (half the base)
⅔ cup lard
¾ cup sugar
1 tsp baking powder and ½ tsp salt
½ cup raisins
1 tsp ground cinnamon
A few drops of red food coloring (the traditional pink) or a little beet juice

steps: Beat the lard until fluffy. Beat in the masa, sugar, baking powder, salt, cinnamon and color until a little ball floats in water.
Fold in the raisins.
Spread on husks with no filling, fold, and steam 1 hour.
